name: Main Street Mornington Festival
tagline: Mornington’s big street-festival day — food, wine, music and Main Street closed to traffic.
summary: Main Street Mornington Festival is the town’s broadest community street festival: local food, wine, beer, cider, spirits, produce, craft, music, kids’ activities and roving performers along Mornington’s main village spine. The event has historically run on the third Sunday in October, though recent funding uncertainty means current-year status must be checked before travel.
heroImageAlt: Local produce and market stalls on the Mornington Peninsula
whatItIs:
A free, family-friendly street festival staged along Main Street Mornington, combining local food and wine, craft beer and cider, market stalls, local produce, music, kids’ activity and street performance. The organiser describes it as an annual event traditionally held on the third Sunday in October, with multiple stages and performance areas and a large day-visitor crowd.

The caveat matters: the 2025 edition was cancelled and the organiser site is seeking sponsors for 2026. This page therefore treats the festival as a Signature Event in the Peninsula calendar, not as a confirmed current-year listing.
whoItsFor: Families, local residents, Mornington day-trippers, market browsers and visitors who want a low-barrier Peninsula day without ticketing or a formal itinerary. It is best approached as a whole-town street day: wander, eat, watch a set, walk down to the foreshore, then decide whether to stay for dinner.
peninsulaCalendarContext: Gives Mornington a spring civic anchor, distinct from the wine-country weekends in Red Hill and the summer events at Portsea. It belongs in the Signature Events mix because it uses the town itself as the venue and pulls together food, wine, music, craft and family programming in one walkable strip.
gettingThere: Mornington is the easiest of the major Peninsula towns to reach from Melbourne: usually 60–75 minutes in clear traffic via Peninsula Link. On festival days, expect road closures around Main Street and use foreshore or edge-of-centre parking, then walk in. The event pairs naturally with Mornington Pier, the foreshore and dinner in town.
editorialNotes: Official site states 2025 cancelled, sponsors sought for 2026; traditional timing third Sunday October, 11am–5pm, 7 stages/performance areas, 20,000+ visitors. Keep visible copy cautious until organiser confirms the next edition.
